title: Who pays, same filter
hook: The factory may pollute. Does the smoke have to stay?

doesNotKnow: that if bargaining is free, the efficient fix happens whoever holds the legal right; only who pays changes

misconception: If the factory has the right to pollute, the pollution continues.
objective: The learner can explain that because the $100 filter saves $300 of smoke damage, the filter is fitted whoever holds the right (the laundry pays between $100 and $300 for it, or the liable factory fits it itself), so the total cost is $100 either way and the right decides only who pays, when bargaining is free.

claims.text: If the factory is liable, it fits the $100-a-year filter rather than pay $300 a year of damages: factory −$100, laundry $0, total −$100 (paying damages would give factory −$300, laundry $0, total −$300).
claims.source: Lesson numbers D = 300, F = 100 (Demo.tsx). min(F, D) = F; re-run in node by ncm-coase, 2026-10-14. Brief claim 1.

claims.text: If the factory has the right to pollute, the laundry gains by paying the factory between $100 and $300 a year to fit the filter: a $200 offer leaves the factory +$100 and the laundry −$200 (better than −$300 of smoke), total −$100; an offer of $50 leaves the factory −$50, so it refuses; an offer of $350 leaves the laundry worse than the $300 smoke, so it won't pay.
claims.source: Deal test in Demo.tsx: offer − F > 0 and −offer > −D. Node re-run (ncm-coase, 2026-10-14): $50 → factory −50, refused; $200 → factory +100, laundry −200, deal; $350 → laundry −350, refused; strict gains on whole dollars from $101 to $299 (closed range $100–$300 with ties). Brief claim 2.

claims.text: Either way the filter is fitted and the total cost is $100; the legal right decides only who pays. This is the Coase theorem, which holds when bargaining is costless.
claims.source: Coase, R. H. (1960), 'The Problem of Social Cost', Journal of Law and Economics 3; Easley and Kleinberg 2010, ch. 24. Stage: both Totals −$100. Brief claim 3; fact-checker to confirm.

claims.text: With costly bargaining or many parties, the Coase result can fail.
claims.source: Easley and Kleinberg 2010, ch. 24. Reveal's last sentence. Brief claim 4; fact-checker to confirm.

claims.text: The lesson is a simplified model: two parties, costless bargaining and known costs; the $300 smoke damage and $100 filter (both a year) are made-up numbers.
claims.source: Lesson rule. Stage line 'Simplified: two sides, free bargaining, costs known.' (visible through the reveal); Demo.tsx constants D, F. Tied to c4.

recall.question: A farm's runoff costs a fishery $500 a year; a fence that stops it costs $200 a year. The farm may legally pollute and bargaining is free. What happens?
options: The runoff continues: the farm has the right
The fishery pays the farm to build the fence
The farm builds the fence at its own cost
recall.why: The fence saves the fishery $500 for $200, so any payment between $200 and $500 leaves both better off; the fence goes up, and the right only decides that the fishery pays.
